transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-13
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Carter (Redwood AE), Marcus Lin (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Redwood CSM), Dr. Anika Reddy (Penumbra Head of AI Ops), Michael Torres (CTO), Jenna Ortiz (Platform Engineer), Luis Moreno (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto): Align on commitment rollforward and region staging. Action items captured.

00:00 Sophie: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you fitting us in today, um quick agenda — commitment rollforward, region staging for EU and APAC pilot, procurement timeline, and then tech benchmark plan.
00:22 Michael: yeah thanks, Sophie. we'll start on our side — high level we want to avoid any gap in capacity as we move into the new fiscal window, and also accelerate APAC latency improvements for our clinical inference.
00:35 Dr. Reddy: and just to be explicit, the main metric we care about is p95 latency for clinical routing under 350ms for the patient-facing flows. cost is important but SLA trumps cost for those endpoints.
00:58 Marcus: got it. so from Redwood's perspective we can do a 20% commitment top-up to cover burst and steady growth, and we have a couple of staging options — dedicated EU cluster, or host in our EU hosted tier with VPC peering.
01:19 Jenna: quick clarifying q — for the EU staging, will that be a full private control plane or a shared control plane with VPC peering? there's compliance implications.
01:35 Marcus: right, good call. we recommend private control plane if you need strict audit and isolation; if you can tolerate shared control plane (hosted) with strict network controls and customer-side peering, that moves faster.
01:52 Michael: timeline wise procurement will need a formal SOW and numbers. Luis, any initial thoughts?
02:03 Luis: we'll need an itemized cost sheet; procurement also wants an appendix for audit and SOC 2 evidence. if we can get that in the next week it helps the internal cadence.
02:18 Sophie: absolutely. i'll take the pricing spreadsheet and SOW action. expect initial draft by mid next week.
02:30 Marcus: for the benchmark, we'd like to run two quick passes: your production-like sample traffic for p95/p50 and throughput for a sustained 30-minute run, and then a short failover test to confirm KV cache rehydration.
02:49 Dr. Reddy: can you do the failover test without touching our production routing? we prefer staged tests.
03:00 Marcus: yes, totally — test in staging with same data shape. we can simulate the regional failover via our routing rules.
03:12 Michael: about the rollforward, legal asked about the mechanism — do we sign a new contract or an amendment that rolls numbers forward?
03:21 Sophie: typically we do an amendment that extends the term and sets the new reserved capacity — keeps existing terms intact. legal loves that because it avoids full renegotiation. but we can also do a new SOW if you prefer.
03:36 Jenna: curious on autoscaling under reserved capacity — how aggressive is the burst? we have traffic spikes tied to monthly batch jobs.
03:46 Marcus: autoscaling for Dedicated is configurable. we can set a buffer for steady autoscale and also a controlled burst pool — that burst pool is limited by policy and can be priced as overage or pre-bought credits.
04:02 Dr. Reddy: what's the impact to latency when a request routes from us-west to EU — ballpark?
04:10 Marcus: ballpark p95 delta 60 to 120ms depending on region and path; for APAC it's larger, often 120–200ms. but if you stage model replicas in region you get near-local latencies.
04:27 Michael: so for patient flows we likely need EU replicas. we can't accept 200ms extra.
04:33 Sophie: agreed. suggested plan — EU replicate for patient-facing routes, APAC pilot for internal analytics first.
04:44 Luis: procurement question — do you support invoice net-45? our policy is net-30 but we can discuss.
04:52 Sophie: yes we can be flexible, that's a commercial item — i'll note for finance.
04:58 Marcus: security — KMS/HSM integration: if Penumbra wants to bring-your-own-key, we support KMS integrations and for on-prem HSM there are options via our private deployment; there's some onboarding work to validate key wrapping and rotation.
05:15 Jenna: do you have an integration guide?
05:19 Marcus: yes, i'll share the KMS integration doc and a short runbook.
05:24 Dr. Reddy: also need SSO — SAML, SCIM and RBAC mapping so our ops team can manage keys.
05:31 Marcus: we do SAML SSO and SCIM; RBAC granularity down to token-level and route-level.
05:38 Sophie: quick commercial note — if you commit to the 20% top-up for 12 months we can offer a stepped discount and include a one-time region activation credit for EU.
05:52 Michael: what's the activation lead time for the EU cluster?
05:56 Marcus: if you go hosted EU with peering 5–7 business days after PO; private control plane or on-prem adds 3–6 weeks depending on network reviews.
06:10 Dr. Reddy: ok that's clear. i'd like to see a short runbook for EU failover and fallback policy.
06:17 Marcus: yep, we have a failover playbook template. we'll paper that into the SOW appendix.
06:24 Sophie: action item summary — i'll send pricing and SOW. Marcus will run benchmark. Jenna will send traffic profile. Luis will confirm procurement timing. Anika will finalize residency.
06:40 Michael: sounds good. any blockers from Redwood side?
06:44 Marcus: none besides access to the test dataset and sample traces.
06:50 Dr. Reddy: we'll provision a sanitized sample set and a VPN account for staging.
07:00 Marcus: perfect, that should let us replicate cache behavior and KV hit ratios.
07:08 Sophie: timeline recap: pricing & SOW by 8/18, benchmark week of 8/17, KMS decision by 8/20, procurement ETA by 8/25.
07:21 Luis: note we may need legal to review the amendment. can you include a short redline-friendly amendment draft?
07:31 Sophie: yes — i'll send an amendment template so legal can redline.
07:36 Marcus: technical detail — for throughput testing we'll test both baseline and 8-bit quantized variants. on some of your models quantization saves 30–50% tokens cost with small latency difference.
07:53 Jenna: that's helpful, our secondary models are tolerant to quantization.
07:58 Dr. Reddy: anything else on SLOs? we want an SLA for p99 availability and a clear runbook for incident escalation.
08:08 Ravi: i'll coordinate the SLA appendix; we have standard SLOs and incident escalation templates and can adapt them to your oncall.
08:18 Michael: good. do you have any references for similar clinical customers?
08:23 Sophie: we can share anonymized case studies and a contact reference under NDA if needed.
08:29 Michael: ok let's do that.
08:33 Sophie: last check — competitors mentioned LargeCloudX earlier by Penumbra?
08:36 Dr. Reddy: they've been mentioned in procurement; LargeCloudX offered a global footprint but at a higher cost.
08:44 Marcus: noted, we'll make sure to highlight predictable economics in the materials.
08:49 Sophie: alright, wrapping — i'll send the list of deliverables and a meeting recap. Marcus will set up the benchmark invite and include expected metrics. Ravi will track the action items.
09:05 Michael: thanks folks. we'll look for the docs and benchmark schedule.
09:10 Sophie: thanks everyone, talk soon. bye.

End of transcript.
